paper.title: Decentralized Contextual Bandits with Network Adaptivity

settings.name_in_paper: Networked (decentralized) linear contextual bandits with shared and node-specific features (benchmark analysis)
unmapped: N agents each solve a K-armed disjoint linear contextual bandit; each arm has its own parameter theta_i^k = [theta_c^k, theta_{i,s}^k] whose first d_c coordinates are shared across all nodes and the remaining d_{i,s} are node-specific
Regret summed over all N nodes
settings.definition_quote:
For each node \(i\) and arm \(a^{(k)}\), the reward is modeled as a linear function of the context, \(
r_{i,t}^k = \mathbf{x}_{i,t}^\top \theta_i^k + \epsilon_{i,t}^k\), where \( \epsilon_{i,t}^k \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_k^2) \) is zero-mean Gaussian noise. The expected reward is therefore 
\(\mathbb{E}[r_{i,t}^k \mid \mathbf{x}_{i,t}] = \mathbf{x}_{i,t}^\top \theta_i^k\).

settings.name_in_paper: Networked (decentralized) linear contextual bandits with shared and node-specific features, i.i.d. contexts (NetLinUCB / Net-SGD-UCB analysis)
unmapped: N agents each solve a K-armed disjoint linear contextual bandit; per-arm parameters split into a d_c-dimensional part shared across nodes and a d_{i,s}-dimensional node-specific part
Regret summed over all N nodes
Context covariance has minimum eigenvalue bounded below by a context-diversity constant c > 0
settings.definition_quote: In the LinUCB setting, the context vectors are bounded, i.i.d., and span the feature space, which implies that the population covariance matrix ... is full-rank with lambda_min > 0.

symbols.sum_d_s: sum over nodes of node-specific dimensions, sum_i d_{i,s}

source.label: prop:wholelinucb
source.quote: The total cumulative regret of Shared LinUCB over the network satisfies $R(T) = O\left((d_c + \sum_{i=1}^{N} d_{i,s}) \sqrt{T \log T} \right).$

results.notes: Benchmark; paper says it extends Das & Sinha (2024). Proof only a sketch. Regret defined as difference of expected rewards (pseudo-regret).

symbols.c_div: context-diversity constant: lower bound on the minimum eigenvalue of the normalized empirical context covariance

conditions: contexts i.i.d. and spanning the feature space with lambda_min of normalized empirical covariance >= c > 0

source.label: thm:netlinucb-regret
source.quote: The cumulative regret of the common component in the network is O(\sqrt{\frac{d_cT N}{c} \log (\frac{cTN}{d_c})}) ... The cumulative regret of the node-specific component is O( \sum_{i=1}^{N} d_{i, s} \sqrt{T \log T}). Thus, the overall cumulative regret R(T) of the NetLinUCB algorithm is O( \sqrt{\frac{d_cT N}{c} \log (\frac{cTN}{d_c})} + \sum_{i=1}^{N} d_{i, s} \sqrt{T \log T} ).

results.notes: Theorem also states the shared and node-specific components separately; recorded the total. Proof has a factor sqrt(K) and (1+eta) that are absorbed/dropped in the O; the argument is heuristic. Probability type not explicit; derived from high-probability confidence bounds.

source.label: prop:sgd-ucb-regret-bound
source.quote: Under the conditions of Proposition~\ref{prop:grad-bound}, bounded contexts x_t, and sub-Gaussian noise epsilon_t with variance sigma^2. With a probability of at least 1 - 1/T, the cumulative regret of Net-SGD-UCB in a single node is bounded by R(T) \leq 2\alpha^{sgd}( \frac{\sqrt{2dT \log (\sigma^2 T)}}{(1 - \gamma)\sigma} + \sigma \sqrt{\frac{(1 - \mu)T\log T}{(1 + \mu)(1 - \gamma)}} ), where \alpha^{sgd} \propto 1 + \sigma^2

results.notes: Per-node bound; d is the context dimension of the node. Proof is heuristic (mixes expectation and high probability).

bound.expression: sqrt(N*d_c*T*log(sigma**2*T))/(1 - gamma_ema) + sum_sqrt_d_s*sqrt(2*T*log(sigma**2*T))/((1 - gamma_ema)*sigma) + sigma*N*sqrt((1 - mu_mom)*T*log(T)/((1 + mu_mom)*(1 - gamma_ema)))
bound.expression_latex: R_1(T) = O( \frac{\sqrt{ N d_c T \log (\sigma^2 T})}{1 - \gamma} ),\ R_2(T) = O ( \sum_{i=1}^N \frac{\sqrt{2d_{i,s}T \log (\sigma^2 T)}}{(1 - \gamma)\sigma} + \sigma N \sqrt{\frac{(1 - \mu)T\log T}{(1 + \mu)(1 - \gamma)}} )

source.label: thm:sgd-ucb-network-regret
source.quote: In the Net-SGD-UCB framework, the cumulative regret decomposes into a shared and a node-specific component. The shared component scales as R_1(T) = O( \frac{\sqrt{ N d_c T \log (\sigma^2 T})}{1 - \gamma} ). The node-specific regret satisfies R_2(T) = O ( \sum_{i=1}^N \frac{\sqrt{2d_{i,s}T \log (\sigma^2 T)}}{(1 - \gamma)\sigma} + \sigma N \sqrt{\frac{(1 - \mu)T\log T}{(1 + \mu)(1 - \gamma)}} ).

results.notes: Theorem states shared and node-specific components separately; recorded their sum R_1 + R_2 as the total regret. Probability type not explicit. Proof is heuristic.
